```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
library(FruitTrait)
```

FruitTrait measures the colour of single fleshy fruits of trees, shrubs and woody climbers in field photographs.
The photo pipeline (detection, outlines, outline checks and fruit classifiers) runs in an optional 'Python' back
end; everything in this vignette except the last section runs in R alone, on the example photos and validation
data shipped with the package.

## Scope

`fr_in_scope()` tells whether a species belongs to the group for which the method was built (`fr_scope`), and
`fr_taxonomy()` matches names to the GBIF backbone:

```{r}
fr_in_scope(c("Sorbus aucuparia", "Malus sylvestris", "Fragaria vesca"))
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fr_taxonomy(c("Sorbus aucuparia", "Viburnum opulus"))
```

## Example photos and their outlines

Eight research-grade iNaturalist photos (CC0 or CC BY 4.0) are shipped with the crops and fruit label maps written
by the back end:

```{r}
ex <- fr_example_photos()
ex[, c("photo_id", "species", "family", "rights_holder", "license")]
```

```{r, fig.height = 3.6}
op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
fr_plot_fruits(ex$crop[1], ex$labels[1], main = ex$species[1])
fr_plot_fruits(ex$crop[5], ex$labels[5], main = ex$species[5])
par(op)
```

The colour of outlined fruits is recomputed in R from a crop and its label map, for example after an outline has
been corrected by hand. Each fruit's colour is the mean CIELAB (D65) colour of its pixels without the brightest 2%,
which are mostly specular highlights:

```{r}
fr_fruit_colour(ex$crop[1], ex$labels[1])
fr_fruit_colour(ex$crop[1], ex$labels[1], white_balance = "gray_world")[, c("label", "L", "a", "b", "name")]
```

Colour casts, clipping and dark crops are flagged by `fr_colour_check()`:

```{r}
fr_colour_check(ex$crop, ex$labels)
```

## Results of the back end and decision rules

`fr_example_results()` returns the back-end results for the example photos. A fruit is measurable when its outline
passed the checks and the classifiers rate it a single fruit with a correct outline (`p_valid` at least 0.5) and
ripe (`p_ripe` at least 0.5); the colour of a photo (`m_L`, `m_a`, `m_b`, `m_C`, `m_hue`, `m_name`) is the mean colour
of its measurable fruits.

```{r}
res <- fr_example_results(rule = "measurable")
res[, c("photo_id", "species", "n_fruits_ok", "m_n", "m_name", "v_name", "keep")]
summary(res)
f <- fr_fruits(res, "outlined")
head(f[, c("photo_id", "label", "px", "solidity", "p_valid", "p_ripe", "L", "a", "b", "name")])
```

`fr_filter()` applies one of four rules: `"measurable"` (default), `"valid"` (all single fruits with a correct
outline, ripe or not), `"outlined"` (all outlines that passed the checks) and `"none"`. The precision and recall of
the classifiers at several thresholds were estimated on the rated benchmark fruits with out-of-fold
predictions:

```{r}
fr_benchmark$heads[, c("head", "fruits", "cv_auc", "oof_balanced_accuracy", "nested_cv_auc", "usable")]
round(fr_benchmark$rules, 3)
```

The ripeness classifier keeps ripe red, black and blue fruits more often than ripe yellow, orange and brown fruits,
so analyses of colour composition should be repeated with the colour of all valid fruits (`v_` traits):

```{r}
rc <- fr_benchmark$ripe_colour
rc[rc$rated == "ripe", ]
```

## How far can each trait be trusted?

`fr_catalogue` lists every trait with its definition, its repeatability between two photos of the same plant
(`fr_validation`), its invariance to simulated camera changes and resolution, and a verdict:

```{r}
table(fr_catalogue$family, fr_catalogue$verdict)
fr_trait_info(c("m_L", "m_a", "m_b", "m_C", "m_hue", "m_name"))
fr_reliable_traits(c("reliable", "use with care"))
```

Repeatability is the intraclass correlation ICC(1) between two photos of the same plant taken on the same
occasion, with a bootstrap interval over observations:

```{r, fig.height = 3.4}
v <- fr_validation[fr_validation$both_measurable, ]
r <- fr_repeatability(v, traits = c("m_L", "m_a", "m_b", "m_C", "m_hue", "ring_dE00", "gloss_frac"), boot = 100)
r
fr_plot_repeatability(r)
```

`fr_augment()` simulates camera changes (white balance, exposure, JPEG compression, blur, rotation, perspective) and
training-style augmentations (quarter turns, mirroring, colour jitter); `fr_invariance()` measures how much the fruit
colour changes under them and when the fruits are reduced to a given size, and `fr_augment_check()` expresses the
change relative to the usual difference between photos:

```{r}
inv <- fr_invariance(ex$crop, ex$labels, types = c("white_balance", "exposure", "jpeg"), rungs = 32, min_n = 5)
round(inv, 3)
chk <- fr_augment_check(ex$crop[1], ex$labels[1], types = c("rotate90", "saturation", "hue"))
chk[chk$trait %in% c("L", "C", "hue_deg"), c("type", "trait", "mean_change", "rel_change", "flag")]
```

The results of these analyses on the benchmark crops are in `fr_benchmark$invariance` and
`fr_benchmark$augmentation`.

## Photo colour against reflectance spectra

`fr_spectra_to_lab()` converts reflectance spectra to the colour space of the traits (CIE 1931 2° observer, D65):

```{r}
wl <- 300:700
red_fruit <- 4 + 60 / (1 + exp(-(wl - 600) / 10))
fr_spectra_to_lab(wl, red_fruit)
```

`fr_reference` holds the mean photo colour of 104 species with published fruit reflectance spectra:

```{r, fig.height = 3.6}
with(fr_reference, cor.test(C, spectral_saturation, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE))
plot(spectral_saturation ~ C, data = fr_reference, pch = 19, col = "grey30",
     xlab = "Chroma C* of the photographs", ylab = "Spectral saturation")
```

## Reading the published data set

The tables of the FruitTraits data set are read with the column types of its data dictionary: only empty fields
are missing values, so that the country code of Namibia (`"NA"`) is kept.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
photos <- fr_read_dataset("PATH_TO_DATASET_FOLDER", "photos")
fruits <- fr_read_dataset("PATH_TO_DATASET_FOLDER", "fruits")
```

## A complete analysis with the back end

```{r, eval = FALSE}
fr_install(cpu_only = TRUE)        # once
fr_use_backend()                   # in every R session
ph <- fr_inat_photos("Sorbus aucuparia", n = 50)
ph <- fr_download_photos(ph, dir = "PATH_TO_PHOTO_FOLDER")
res <- fr_process(ph, out_dir = "PATH_TO_OUTPUT_FOLDER")
summary(res)
fr_contact_sheet(res)              # check outlines by eye
fr_summarise(res)                  # colour per species
writeLines(fr_attribution(ph), "attribution.txt")
```
